sections.h2: What is Coffee County, Georgia like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Coffee County sits in south Georgia's Wiregrass region, with Douglas as the county seat and largest city. The county was created in 1854 and covers 603 square miles, of which 575 are land. Besides Douglas, the incorporated cities are Ambrose, Broxton and Nicholls. South Georgia State College, the oldest two-year school in the University System of Georgia, is in Douglas.

The 2020 census counted 43,092 residents and 15,277 households, with a median age of 36.6. There were 17,331 housing units, and 11.9% of them were vacant. Of the occupied homes, 63.9% were owner-occupied and 36.1% were rented. Sellers with acreage should look at the land programs described below before they list.

Local landmarks include the Broxton Rocks sandstone outcrops, General Coffee State Park at 1,490 acres, and Mule Day, held the second Saturday in November.

sections.h2: Which Coffee County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The work is split between two offices. The Coffee County Tax Assessors Office sets values and takes appeals. It is at 224 West Ashley Street, Suite C, in Douglas, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, at 912-384-2136, with a personal property line at 912-493-1100.

The Tax Commissioner bills and collects the tax and takes homestead applications. The main office is at 224 Ashley Street West, Suite B, in Douglas, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:50 p.m., at (912) 384-4895. The mailing address is P.O. Box 1207, Douglas, GA 31533. Property taxes can be paid online through the commissioner's site, which is run on a vendor's platform. Anyone with a question about a bill should call the commissioner. The assessors' own page says they establish values only.

Georgia cities levy their own ad valorem tax, and in some counties the Tax Commissioner collects it on the same bill. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a parcel in Douglas, Broxton, Nicholls or Ambrose gets one bill or two.

sections.h2: What are the key property tax deadlines in Coffee County?
sections.html:
The assessors' page prints the dates owners need most. April 1 is the filing deadline for homestead exemptions, personal property returns and the conservation use, preferential and forest land programs, and the same programs can also be applied for during the appeal window. A homestead exemption has to be in place for the January 1 owner, and you must still own and occupy the home on that date.

Coffee County filing and appeal dates printed by the Tax Assessors Office
ItemDate
Homestead exemption filingJanuary 1 to April 1
Personal property returnApril 1
Conservation use, preferential and forest land applicationsApril 1, or during the appeal window
2026 assessment notices mailedAugust 4, 2026
2026 appeal deadlineSeptember 18, 2026 (passed)

The county has also announced a review of every parcel over a three-year stretch, using contract appraisers from GMASS who carry ID badges and drive marked vehicles. State law requires notice before an appraiser visits a property that changed hands in the last 12 months, took out a building permit, reported fire damage or demolition, or filed an appeal. Most of these field visits take place between January 1 and May 1.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Coffee County assessment?
sections.html:
The window is 45 days from the date of the notice, which is why the 2026 window ran from the August 4 mailing to September 18. Real property owners are encouraged to use the appeals module on the county's qPublic site, and computers are available in the assessors' lobby. Personal property appeals are different: they must be in writing, and mailed ones need a postmark by the deadline.

After the Board of Tax Assessors reviews the appeal, it either changes the value or forwards the case to the County Board of Equalization, which holds a hearing and issues a decision. An owner who is still unhappy can go to Superior Court, or choose arbitration in place of the Board of Equalization. Appeals can be based on taxability, value or uniformity with similar properties. A complaint about the size of the tax bill is not a valid ground.

If the notice never arrived, call the assessors to confirm your mailing address. The assessors say a notice obtained from their office serves as your official notice if the mailed copy never came.

sections.h2: What exemptions and programs does Coffee County list?
sections.html:
The homestead application is filed with the Tax Commissioner between January 1 and April 1 for the year the exemption first applies. Once granted, it renews each year until ownership changes or the owner qualifies for a different kind. The county's exemptions page lists these items:

  • A standard homestead exemption.
  • A $4,000 exemption for owners 65 or older.
  • An added school tax exemption for owners 62 or older whose household income stays under the limit printed on the page, up to $10,000 of assessed value.
  • A $50,000 exemption for qualifying disabled veterans, extended to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.
  • A tax deferral program for homestead owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less. Deferred tax is due when ownership changes or when the deferred amount plus interest reaches 85% of the property's fair market value.

Amounts on the county page can change with state law, so confirm each one with the Tax Commissioner before you rely on it. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant, when the legislature funds it, appears as a credit on the bill.

Land owners have more options. Certain agricultural property can be assessed at 30% instead of 40% of fair market value. Conservation use assessment requires a 10-year covenant and a $10.00 recording fee with the application. Breaking the covenant carries a penalty of twice the taxes saved, plus interest at 1% a month if the break is not reported. A buyer who keeps the use can take over the covenant by signing it.

sections.h2: When are Coffee County property taxes due and what if they are late?
sections.html:
The default state due date is December 20, though a local government may move it to December 1 or November 15, or use installment billing. Coffee County's due date can change from year to year, so ask the Tax Commissioner for the date on your bill. Georgia gives each taxpayer 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, and late balances can also pick up penalties.

A refund for tax that was wrongly assessed must be requested in writing within three years of payment. For an appealed value, the refund is processed automatically once the final value is set. Unpaid balances can lead to a lien and a tax sale, and a title company will want those cleared at closing.

If the house also sits on the Coffee County conservation use covenant, mention that to your closing attorney as well, because a sale to a buyer who will change the use can trigger the penalty.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a Coffee County house?
sections.html:
Taxes are assessed to the January 1 owner and billed to the owner of record, and the sales contract and settlement statement divide the year between buyer and seller. Ask the closing attorney to get a payoff from the Tax Commissioner at (912) 384-4895 and to include any city bill. After closing, remove your homestead exemption by telling the commissioner, and let the buyer know they must apply on their own, with April 1 as the filing deadline.

  • Confirm the current balance and whether a city bill also applies.
  • Ask whether the parcel is in conservation use, since the covenant affects a buyer.
  • Check whether a homestead exemption will need to be dropped.
  • Keep the closing statement as proof that taxes were paid.

A house with deferred maintenance, tenants or back taxes can be harder to sell on the open market. A cash buyer who buys as-is skips the lender's appraisal and can close around the tax payoff.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property taxes in Coffee County, Georgia?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at (912) 384-4895 for bills, payments and homestead applications. Call the Tax Assessors Office at 912-384-2136 for values and appeals. The assessors say they set values only, so tax bill questions belong with the commissioner.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Coffee County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1. Filing runs January 1 through April 1 of the year the exemption first applies, and you must own and occupy the home on January 1. The application goes to the Tax Commissioner. A late application generally waits for the next tax year.

faqs.q: Did Coffee County's 2026 appeal window close?
faqs.a: Yes. Assessment notices were mailed August 4, 2026, and the last day to appeal was September 18, 2026. Real property owners were encouraged to use the qPublic appeals module. In later years the window is 45 days from the notice date, so check the date printed on your notice.

faqs.q: Does Coffee County conservation use transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: It can. If the buyer keeps the land in the same qualifying use and signs the covenant, no penalty applies. If the use changes during the 10-year period, the penalty of twice the taxes saved applies. Tell your closing attorney if your parcel is enrolled.

faqs.q: What happens to Coffee County taxes at closing?
faqs.a: The closing attorney or title company pays the balance from your proceeds, including any city bill. Taxes follow the January 1 owner, and the contract splits the year between you and the buyer. Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner for your closing date.
